preconditions.description: Input s must be a string and k must be an integer.
The length of string s is between 1 and 10^5 inclusive.
The integer k is between 1 and the length of s inclusive.

postconditions.expression: all(s.count(c) % k != 0 or s.count(c) == 0 for c in set(return_value))
postconditions.description: This clause is a placeholder for the complex reduction logic; the actual postcondition is defined by the process: the returned string is the result of repeatedly removing any k consecutive identical characters until no such group exists.

postconditions.expression: not any(return_value[i] == return_value[i+1] for i in range(len(return_value)-1) if all(return_value[j] == return_value[i] for j in range(i, min(i+k, len(return_value)))))
postconditions.description: The returned string contains no group of k consecutive identical characters.
The returned string is the unique result of applying the reduction operation until no further reductions are possible, regardless of the order of operations.
